topics.topic: Complex number as an ordered pair
topics.real_world_problem: The signal arrives as two raw numbers per burst with no label — the crew cannot tell if it is one quantity or two independent readings.
topics.why_this_tool: Ordered pairs are the minimum structure to treat two readings as one object you can compare and manipulate.
topics.core_visual_idea: Two numbers on separate axes slide together to become one point — one object, not two numbers.

topics.real_world_problem: The ship computer cannot log raw pairs — it needs a format compatible with existing algebra routines.
topics.why_this_tool: Same object as $(a,b)$ written so ordinary symbolic algebra applies directly.
topics.core_visual_idea: The point $(a,b)$ relabels as $a+ib$ on the same plane — translation, not a new object.
